structure_policy.notes: The source has a work title but no internal section headings; the three section nodes are inferred from paragraph-level discourse shifts.

nodes.title: Why Definitions Matter in Disagreement
nodes.summary: The essay argues that conceptual clarification can be a prerequisite for evaluating reasons in some disputes.

nodes.title: Problem: apparent disagreement may conceal different questions
nodes.summary: The opening motivates the need to distinguish kinds of disagreement.
nodes.role_in_parent: Creates the problem that the conceptual distinction will solve.

nodes.title: Distinction: verbal versus substantive disagreement
nodes.summary: The essay defines a distinction that diagnoses whether disagreement persists after clarification.
nodes.role_in_parent: Supplies the conceptual tool needed to resolve the opening problem.

nodes.title: Consequence: clarification can precede evaluation of reasons
nodes.summary: The final paragraph derives a methodological consequence for the order of argument.
nodes.role_in_parent: Turns the distinction into the essay's practical thesis about argumentative order.

edges.explanation: The diagnostic distinction in section 2 is introduced to answer the problem identified in section 1.
The methodological conclusion in section 3 depends on the verbal/substantive distinction established in section 2.
The distinction explains why clarification can have priority over evaluating reasons in disputes that may be merely verbal.
edges.notes: Retained in addition to requires because it captures an argumentative role, not only a prerequisite relation.
